To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) PRAM can be a viable candidate for future 3D-stacked memory architectures; (2) 3D integration technology is a key enabler for the power savings of PRAM; and (3) OS- and architecture-level optimizations can further improve PRAM performance and lifetime.

3D-stacked PRAM can be used to alleviate the power/thermal challenges of the upcoming technology nodes, and that the unique characteristics of PRAM allow for the development of a hybrid memory system that achieves high performance, low power, and long lifetime.

3D die stacking is a promising technology for future memory system architecture, and PRAM is a promising candidate for 3D memory architecture because of its unique, heat- driven programming mechanism.

the development of novel memory architectures that are scalable to the 22-nm technology node and beyond.
the design and analysis of emerging memory architectures for future 3D chip designs.
